{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BnJAaaufsxuQFhckybtZje","type":"tool_result","content":"     5 mdparser/__init__.py\n   422 mdparser/blocks.py\n    49 mdparser/cli.py\n    96 mdparser/entities.py\n   602 mdparser/inlines.py\n    87 mdparser/links.py\n   250 mdparser/refs.py\n    71 mdparser/render.py\n    13 tests/conftest.py\n   250 tests/test_atx_headings.py\n   271 tests/test_autolinks.py\n   169 tests/test_backslash_escapes.py\n   113 tests/test_block_engine.py\n   346 tests/test_blocks.py\n   198 tests/test_code_spans.py\n   277 tests/test_emphasis.py\n   316 tests/test_entities.py\n   222 tests/test_executable.py\n    90 tests/test_foundation.py\n   265 tests/test_images.py\n   253 tests/test_line_breaks.py\n   414 tests/test_link_reference_definitions.py\n   358 tests/test_links.py\n   243 tests/test_raw_html.py\n   131 tests/test_render.py\n   187 tests/test_thematic_breaks.py\n  5698 total\n\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n        tip = self.root\n        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n            tip = child\n        return tip\n\n    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n        child = container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n        block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters.\"\"\"\n    parser = DocumentParser(registry)\n    for line in lines:\n        parser.incorporate_line(line)\n The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\"\"\"\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, lambda raw: inlines.parse_inline(raw, root.references))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01L2PpJMJMf6uxeuELFMcfoM","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"ATX heading tests: the six declared checks from FEATURE-ATX-Headings.md, then block-tree and\nexact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import ATX_HEADING, PARAGRAPH, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, source: str) -> str:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-ATX-Headings.md) ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"level\", range(1, 7))\ndef test_atx_levels_one_to_six(project_root: Path, level: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Each opening-sequence length from 1 to 6 renders exactly one heading of that level.\"\"\"\n    source = \"#\" * level + \" foo\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\" + str(level) + \">\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_atx_not_a_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Seven hashes, a missing space, and an escaped hash do not produce headings.\"\"\"\n    source = \"####### foo\\n\\n#hashtag\\n\\n\\\\## foo\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 3\n\n\ndef test_atx_closing_sequence(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A closing hash sequence is removed from the heading content.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"## foo ##\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_atx_empty_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Empty headings are allowed, one per line.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"#\\n\\n##\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_atx_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A heading splits a paragraph without blank lines, leaving two paragraphs around it.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo bar\\n# baz\\nBar foo\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_atx_indentation_limit(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Up to three spaces of indentation are allowed before the opening sequence, and four are not.\"\"\"\n    allowed = run_commonmark(project_root, \"   # foo\\n\")\n    refused = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    # foo\\n\")\n    print(allowed.stdout)\n    print(refused.stdout)\n    assert allowed.returncode == 0\n    assert refused.returncode == 0\n    assert allowed.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert refused.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n\n\n# --- Block tree: opening sequence ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"level\", range(1, 7))\ndef test_opening_run_of_each_length_is_a_heading(level: int) -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"#\" * level + \" foo\"]) == [ATX_HEADING.name]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"level\", range(1, 7))\ndef test_heading_block_records_its_level(level: int) -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"#\" * level + \" foo\"]).children\n    assert block.level == level\n\n\ndef test_seven_hashes_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"####### foo\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_hash_without_following_space_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"#hashtag\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_hash_followed_by_tab_is_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"#\\tfoo\"]) == [ATX_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_lone_hash_is_an_empty_heading() -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"#\"]).children\n    assert block.kind is ATX_HEADING\n    assert block.level == 1\n    assert block.content == \"\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"indent\", [1, 2, 3])\ndef test_up_to_three_spaces_of_indentation_form_a_heading(indent: int) -> None:\n    assert kinds([\" \" * indent + \"# foo\"]) == [ATX_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_four_spaces_of_indentation_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"    # foo\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_one_tab_of_indentation_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"\\t# foo\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_escaped_hash_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"\\\\# foo\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\n# --- Block tree: content and closing sequence ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"line\", \"content\"),\n    [\n        (\"# foo\", \"foo\"),\n        (\"#   foo   \", \"foo\"),\n        (\"#\\tfoo\\t\", \"foo\"),\n        (\"# foo ##\", \"foo\"),\n        (\"# foo #\", \"foo\"),\n        (\"# foo ##   \", \"foo\"),\n        (\"# a blank-only document gives no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    word = \"content\"\n    padded = \"\\n  \\n\\n\" + word + \"\\n\\n\\n  \\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, padded)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n    blank = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n \\n\\t\\n\")\n    assert blank.returncode == 0\n    assert blank.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_engine_html_escaping(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Special characters in paragraph text are escaped, so only the paragraph tags contribute angle brackets.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"x < y > z & w\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\">\") == 2\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the executable ---\n\n\ndef test_single_paragraph_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"hello world\\n\").stdout == \"<p>hello world</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_two_paragraphs_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"one\\n\\ntwo\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>one</p>\\n<p>two</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_multiline_paragraph_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    source = \"first line\\n             second line\\nthird line\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>first line\\nsecond line\\nthird line</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_escaped_paragraph_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"x < y > z & w\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>x &lt; y &gt; z &amp; w</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_padded_document_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n  \\n\\ncontent\\n\\n\\n  \\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>content</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_blank_only_document_output_is_empty(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n \\n\\t\\n\").stdout == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_leading_and_trailing_whitespace_is_removed(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"   \\tword \\t  \\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>word</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_crlf_document_renders_the_same_as_lf(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    lf = run_commonmark(project_root, \"one\\ntwo\\n\\nthree\\n\")\n    crlf = run_commonmark(project_root, \"one\\r\\ntwo\\r\\n\\r\\nthree\\r\\n\")\n    assert lf.stdout == crlf.stdout == \"<p>one\\ntwo</p>\\n<p>three</p>\\n\"\n#!/bin/bash\n# CommandCenter Operation\n# Name: Run Test Suite\n# Type: batch\n\n# --- Standard Preamble ---\nset -euo pipefail\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\nPROJECT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$SCRIPT_DIR/..\" && pwd)\"\nLOG_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/data/logs\"\nmkdir -p \"$LOG_DIR\"\n\nTIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S')\nSCRIPT_NAME=$(basename \"$0\" .sh)\nLOG_FILE=\"$LOG_DIR/${SCRIPT_NAME}_${TIMESTAMP}.log\"\n\necho \"=== $SCRIPT_NAME started at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ===\" | tee \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"Arguments: $*\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"Working dir: $PROJECT_DIR\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\necho \"---\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n\ncd \"$PROJECT_DIR\"\n\n# --- Test Command (pyproject.toml foundation contract: pytest -q, run inside .venv) ---\nif [ ! -x .venv/bin/python ]; then\n    echo \"error: .venv missing; run 'uv venv .venv && uv sync' first\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \"$@\" 2>&1 | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n\necho \"=== $SCRIPT_NAME finished at $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ===\" | tee -a \"$LOG_FILE\"\n[project]\nname = \"mdparser\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"CommonMark 0.31.2 parser: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\ndependencies = []\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\n    \"pytest\",\n]\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\npythonpath = [\".\"]\naddopts = \"-ra\"","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01L2PpJMJMf6uxeuELFMcfoM","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0163chvYg7GywcmMmHSTG1XQ","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Thematic break tests: the four declared checks from FEATURE-Thematic-Breaks.md, then block-tree\nand exact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import PARAGRAPH, THEMATIC_BREAK, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n...\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"indent\", [1, 2, 3])\ndef test_up_to_three_spaces_of_indentation_form_a_break(indent: int) -> None:\n    assert kinds([\" \" * indent + \"***\"]) == [\"thematic_break\"]\n\n\ndef test_four_spaces_of_indentation_is_not_a_break() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"    ***\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_one_tab_of_indentation_is_not_a_break() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"\\t***\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_spaces_and_tabs_between_markers_are_allowed() -> None:\n...\n\n\ndef test_break_line_keeps_no_line_text() -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"- - -   \"]).children\n    assert block.kind is THEMATIC_BREAK\n    assert block.lines == []\n\n\ndef test_indented_marker_run_after_paragraph_is_paragraph_text() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"    ***\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the executable ---\n\n\ndef test_break_renders_as_hr_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"***\\n\").stdout == \"<hr />\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_break_between_paragraphs_renders_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n***\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>Foo</p>\\n<hr />\\n<p>bar</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_consecutive_breaks_render_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"***\\n\\n---\\n\").stdout == \"<hr />\\n<hr />\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_trailing_whitespace_break_renders_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"- - - -    \\t\\n\").stdout == \"<hr />\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_non_break_renders_as_paragraph_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"    ***\\n\").stdout == \"<p>***</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_kind_is_unchanged_by_break_registration() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"plain text\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n...\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"first\\nsecond\\nthird\"]\n\n\ndef test_continuation_lines_drop_their_leading_indentation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"first\", \"      second\", \"\\tthird\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"first\\nsecond\\nthird\"]\n\n\ndef test_first_line_drops_leading_spaces_and_tabs() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"  \\t  word\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\ndef test_final_spaces_and_tabs_are_removed_from_content() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"word \\t  \"])\n\n\n# --- Extensibility: block types registered without changing the loop ---\n\n\ndef _rule_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.strip(\" \\t\") == \"***\":\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RULE)\n    return None\n\n\nRULE = BlockType(\"rule\", continues=lambda block, cursor: False, start=_rule_start)","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d5fa8838-79bf-4c1a-89d4-f52dfb5e23bd","uuid":"d4179bd7-e08e-4c08-9a11-323135d123bf","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:15:12.959Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Thematic break tests: the four declared checks from FEATURE-Thematic-Breaks.md, then block-tree\nand exact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. -   \"]).children\n    assert block.kind is THEMATIC_BREAK\n    assert block.lines == []\n\n\ndef test_indented_marker_run_after_paragraph_is_paragraph_text() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"    ***\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the executable ---\n\n\ndef test_break_renders_as_hr_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"***\\n\").stdout == \"<hr />\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_break_between_paragraphs_renders_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n***\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<p>Foo</p>\\n<hr />\\n<p>bar</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_consecutive_breaks_render_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"***\\n\\n---\\n\").stdout == \"<hr />\\n<hr />\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_trailing_whitespace_break_renders_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"- - - -    \\t\\n\").stdout == \"<hr />\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_non_break_renders_as_paragraph_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"    ***\\n\").stdout == \"<p>***</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_kind_is_unchanged_by_break_registration() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"plain text\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n...\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"first\\nsecond\\nthird\"]\n\n\ndef test_continuation_lines_drop_their_leading_indentation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"first\", \"      second\", \"\\tthird\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"first\\nsecond\\nthird\"]\n\n\ndef test_first_line_drops_leading_spaces_and_tabs() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"  \\t  word\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\ndef test_final_spaces_and_tabs_are_removed_from_content() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"word \\t  \"])\n\n\n# --- Extensibility: block types registered without changing the loop ---\n\n\ndef _rule_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.strip(\" \\t\") == \"***\":\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RULE)\n    return None\n\n\nRULE = BlockType(\"rule\", continues=lambda block, cursor: False, start=_rule_start)","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_0163chvYg7GywcmMmHSTG1XQ","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015Y6ZmJ385zFTzm2czrEvRb","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d5fa8838-79bf-4c1a-89d4-f52dfb5e23bd","uuid":"f7810722-4230-4892-a9f3-ac37c4b7034a","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:15:29.014Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py","oldString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)\n","newString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(INDENTED_CODE)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":68,"oldLines":4,"newStart":68,"newLines":6,"lines":["         return \"<hr />\\n\"","     if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":","         return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"","+    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":","+        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"","     raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01L5X4QZMCEcvnK44bo92Vmn","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.content for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is INDENTED_CODE]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Indented-Code.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_indented_simple_block(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four-space-indented lines render one pre element whose code keeps the extra indentation and content.\"\"\"\n    first = \"a simple\"\n    second = \"  indented code block\"\n    source = \"    \" + first + \"\\n    \" + second + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<code>\") == 1\n    assert first in result.stdout\n    assert second in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_indented_cannot_interrupt_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An indented line directly after paragraph text is a continuation, not a code block.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n    bar\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_indented_chunks_and_ending(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Chunks separated by a blank line form one block, and an unindented line ends it and starts a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    chunk1\\n\\n    chunk2\\nbar\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_indented_content_escaped_and_literal(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Code content is escaped and not parsed as Markdown, so only the four code wrapper tags contribute angle brackets.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    <a/>\\n    *hi*\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<\") == 4\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_indented_tab_indentation(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A leading tab counts as four columns of indentation.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\tfoo\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Block tree: start rule ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"indent\", [4, 5, 8])\ndef test_four_or_more_columns_start_a_code_block(indent: int) -> None:\n test_two_spaces_then_tab_is_four_columns() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"  \\tfoo\"]) == [INDENTED_CODE.name]\n\n\ndef test_three_spaces_then_tab_is_four_columns() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"   \\tfoo\"]) == [INDENTED_CODE.name]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_alone_is_not_a_code_block() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"    \"]) == []\n\n\ndef test_indented_line_after_blank_starts_a_code_block() -> bar\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_indented_line_after_paragraph_does_not_add_a_block() -> None:\n    (paragraph,) = parse_lines([\"Foo\", \"    bar\"]).children\n    assert paragraph.kind is    two extra\"]) == [\"  two extra\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_code_content_keeps_trailing_spaces() -> None:\n    assert code_contents([\"    foo   \"]) == [\"foo   \\n\"]\n\n\ndef assert result.stdout == \"<pre><code>chunk1\\n\\nchunk2\\n</code></pre>\\n<p>bar</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_continuation_renders_exactly(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01C3csZNUnXQ5TLLfPCLMeK8","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_atx_headings.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d5fa8838-79bf-4c1a-89d4-f52dfb5e23bd","uuid":"51a5fd0a-f997-4e96-8615-dd34e026ab0c","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:15:47.414Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_atx_headings.py","oldString":"def test_four_spaces_of_indentation_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"    # foo\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_one_tab_of_indentation_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"\\t# foo\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]","newString":"def test_four_spaces_of_indentation_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"    # foo\"]) == [INDENTED_CODE.name]\n\n\ndef test_one_tab_of_indentation_is_not_a_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"\\t# foo\"]) == [INDENTED_CODE.name]","originalFile":"\"\"\"ATX heading tests: the six declared checks from FEATURE-ATX-Headings.md, then block-tree and\nexact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import ATX_HEADING, PARAGRAPH, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, source: str) -> str:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-ATX-Headings.md) ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"level\", range(1, 7))\ndef test_atx_levels_one_to_six(project_root: Path, level: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Each opening-sequence length from 1 to 6 renders exactly one heading of that level.\"\"\"\n    source = \"#\" * level + \" foo\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\" + str(level) + \">\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_atx_not_a_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Seven hashes, a missing space, and an escaped hash do not produce headings.\"\"\"\n    source = \"####### foo\\n\\n#hashtag\\n\\n\\\\## foo\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 3\n\n\ndef test_atx_closing_sequence(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A closing hash sequence is removed from the heading content.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"## foo ##\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_atx_empty_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Empty headings are allowed, one per line.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"#\\n\\n##\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_atx_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A heading splits a paragraph without blank lines, leaving two paragraphs around it.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo bar\\n# baz\\nBar foo\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_atx_indentation_limit(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Up to three spaces of indentation are allowed before the opening sequence, and four are not.\"\"\"\n    allowed = run_commonmark(project_root, \"   # foo\\n\")\n    refused = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    # foo\\n\")\n    print(allowed.stdout)\n    print(refused.stdout)\n    assert allowed.returncode == 0\n    assert refused.returncode == 0\n    assert allowed.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import ATX_HEADING, PARAGRAPH, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, source: str) -> str:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-ATX-Headings.md) ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"level\", range(1, 7))\ndef test_atx_levels_one_to_six(project_root: Path, level: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Each opening-sequence length from 1 to 6 renders exactly one heading of that level.\"\"\"\n    source = \"#\" * level + \" foo\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\" + str(level) + \">\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_atx_not_a_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Seven hashes, a missing space, and an escaped hash do not produce headings.\"\"\"\n    source = \"####### foo\\n\\n#hashtag\\n\\n\\\\## foo\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 3\n\n\ndef test_atx_closing_sequence(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A closing hash sequence is removed from the heading content.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"## foo ##\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_atx_empty_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Empty headings are allowed, one per line.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"#\\n\\n##\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) hr element.\"\"\"\n    lines = [\"***\", \"---\", \"___\", \"_____________\", \" - - -\", \" **  * ** * ** * **\"]\n    source = \"\\n\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == len(lines)\n\n\ndef test_thematic_not_a_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Wrong characters, too few characters, mixed characters and trailing text do not produce hr elements.\"\"\"\n    source = \"+++\\n\\n--\\n\\n_ _ _ _ a\\n\\na------\\n\\n *-*\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_thematic_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A thematic break directly after paragraph text splits it into two paragraphs around one hr.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n***\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_thematic_trailing_whitespace(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Trailing spaces and tabs after the marker characters are allowed.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"- - - -    \\t\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") Registry tests use block types defined here, which shows that\nthe loop never names a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks\nfrom mdparser.blocks import (\n    DOCUMENT,\n    PARAGRAPH,\n    Block,\n    BlockRegistry,\n    BlockType,\n    Cursor,\n    DocumentParser,\n    indent_columns,\n    next_column,\n    parse_lines,\n)\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_contents(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.content for child in block.children if child.kind is PARAGRAPH]\n\n\n# --- Column helpers ---\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_space_advances_one() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\" \", 3) == 4\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_tab_advances_to_next_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 0) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 2) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 4) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_spaces() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"   x\", 0, 0) == 3\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_expands_a_leading_tab_to_four() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\t\\tx\", 0, 0) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_is_zero_without_leading_whitespace() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"x  \", 0, 0) == 0\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_starts_from_the_given_column() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 2) == 2\n\n\n# --- Cursor ---\n\n\ndef test_cursor_rest_starts_as_the_whole_line() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"abc\").rest == \"abc\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_blank_for_empty_and_whitespace_lines() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\").is_blank()\n    assert Cursor(\" \\t \").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_not_blank_with_text() -> None:\n    assert not Cursor(\"  a\").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_nonspace_tracks_column_across_a_tab() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"  \\t x\")\n test_cursor_advance_columns_stops_at_the_target_column() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"    x\")\n    cursor.advance_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"  x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_indent_reports_columns_to_next_text() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\\t\\tx\").indent == 8\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_to_moves_by_characters() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"abc\")\n    cursor.advance_to(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"c\"\n\n\n# --- Empty and blank input ---\n\n\ndef test_empty_input_gives_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_default_registry_start_rules_are_the_thematic_break_atx_heading_and_indented_code() -> None:\n    assert blocks.DEFAULT_REGISTRY.starts() == (\n        blocks.THEMATIC_BREAK,\n        blocks.ATX_HEADING,\n        blocks.INDENTED_CODE,\n    )\n\n\ndef test_lazy_block_type_must_accept_lines() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        BlockType(\"bad\", continues=lambda block, cursor: True, lazy=True)\n\n\ndef test_leaf_block_type_must_have_an_add_line_rule() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        BlockType(\"bad\", continues=lambda block, cursor: True, accepts_lines=True)\n\n\n# --- Extensibility: block types registered without changing the loop ---\n\n\ndef _rule_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.strip(\" \\t\") == \"***\":\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RULE)\n    return None\n\n\nRULE = BlockType(\"rule\", continues=lambda block, cursor: False, start=_rule_start)\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_interrupts_a_paragraph() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"a\", \"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\", \"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"a\", \"b\"]\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_closes_an_unmatched_block_before_it_starts() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert root.children[0].is_open is False\n\n\ndef _raw_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> test_start_rule_is_not_tried_inside_a_non_interruptible_leaf() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RAW)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"<<\", \"***\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"raw\"]\n    assert root.children[0].lines[-1] == \"***\"\n\n\n# --- Lazy paragraph continuation, via a test-only container
